meta.title: OSS network-quality lake: the journey of one measurement
hero.title: From a phone to the NOC map: one measurement through the lake
hero.lead: A fictional mobile operator's network operations centre (NOC) shows, for the last hour, the 10 cells with the most users and the 10 with the weakest signal. Follow one measurement from a phone and see what each layer changes and how far the row count shrinks.
hero.note: All data is generated in SQL. The operator and the cities are fictional; only the city-centre coordinates are real places in Korea.
where.title: Where this lake sits
where.body: A telco runs two families of systems. BSS handles customers and money (subscriptions, rating, billing); OSS handles the network itself (equipment, faults, quality). This lab is on the OSS side: network-quality data.
where.aria: BSS covers subscriptions, rating and billing; OSS covers equipment, faults and quality. The quality lake sits inside OSS, between the collection of device measurements and the NOC screen.
funnel.title: Fewer rows at every layer
funnel.body: All four layers are ClickHouse tables. The bars are each table's actual row count.
s1.title: A phone sends a measurement
s1.body: The device reports the serving cell's signal strength (RSRP), signal quality (RSRQ, SINR) and channel quality (CQI). The probe tags the location as an H3 res-9 cell (about 170 m a side) and passes the subscriber number (IMSI) on encrypted.
s1.count: {n} measurements a minute across three cities.
s2.title: Bronze keeps it as received
s2.body: Stored without reshaping: H3 as a string, the IMSI as 44 characters of ciphertext, every measurement Nullable. If the cleaning rules change later, everything downstream can be rebuilt from here. A TTL removes it after 3 days.
s3.title: Silver cleans the same row
s3.body: The moment a row lands in bronze, a materialized view rewrites it into silver. Here is the measurement above, before and after.
s3.count: Silver: {n} rows. {d} rows without a cell or a subscriber are dropped; {z} rows without RSRP keep NULL (it is not 0 dBm).
cmp.imsi: ciphertext → hash (cityHash64); the number itself never enters the lake
cmp.dropped: not used by the NOC, dropped
s4.title: Gold folds many rows into one
s4.body: The {n} rows that arrived for one cell in one minute become a single gold row. Users are kept as a uniq state and the rest as sums, so any time range can be merged again.
fold.aria: {n} silver rows fold into 1 gold row
s4.count: Gold: {n} rows (2 hours). The last hour, which the NOC query reads, is {w} rows.
pitfall.title: One pitfall.
pitfall.body: An aggregate state type has to match whether its source column is Nullable. A mismatched MV is refused at CREATE, but if the source column is made Nullable later with ALTER, the ALTER passes and every INSERT after it fails with CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE. The source rows still land, so only gold stops (reproduction in the README).
s5.title: Serving keeps only the 20 rows the screen needs
s5.body: A refreshable materialized view recomputes the last hour from gold every minute and replaces the 20 rows in one swap. The NOC screen reads only these. The highlighted row is the cell our measurement belongs to.
s5.count: Serving: 20 rows, refreshed every minute.
s6.title: The NOC map draws them
s6.body: The 20 serving cells become hexagon outlines with ClickHouse's h3ToGeoBoundary. The shaded hexagons behind them are the last hour's measurement counts (res-7). Busy cells gather downtown; weak ones gather in the coverage holes.
map.nojs: The map is drawn with JavaScript.

same.title: Every layer gives the same 20 rows
same.body: Ask the same NOC question of each of the four layers and the same 20 rows come back (03-queries.sql checks it). What changes is how many rows are read.

cta.title: Send data through it yourself
cta.body: In the live demo, “Send next minute” puts one minute of measurements into bronze; silver and gold counts grow through the MVs, and the 20 serving rows and the map refresh.
cta.note: Needs only Docker and Python 3. Local only, no Cloud cost.

demo.title: Live demo: one minute at a time
demo.lead: Each press puts one minute of measurements into bronze. The MVs carry it into silver and gold, and serving refreshes on the spot. Click a layer to see a sample row and the NOC query asked of that layer.
demo.offline: The demo server or ClickHouse is not reachable. Run ui/up.sh in the lab directory, then open http://localhost:8765/demo .
